answer: An agent economy can resist Sybil attacks by making participation cost bonded stake plus scarce on-chain identity. Each agent must lock funds before its votes count, so faking a thousand personas means posting a thousand bonds. A single verified identity, like a wharf docking a ship once, caps reputational weight per entity. Peers only accept attestations from agents whose stake a bridge across checkpoints, letting new accounts earn trust slowly. No fable of free accounts survives that math.
